brief.headline: Lead with supply-security qualification and faster payment for a modest discount — they're in the grey zone (Altman Z 1.68) and loss-making, so a hard squeeze risks tipping a fragile supplier.

priceAsk.summary: Close the ₹3.91 L annual gap to our best laminate price, targeting ₹290.00/KG on key SKUs
priceAsk.target: ₹290.00/KG on LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 07, LM ELECTRAL UD 4.4g LS 05, and LM ELECTRAL MD 21.80g LS 08 (currently ₹295.00/KG), saving ₹3.91 L per year
priceAsk.basis: Shrinath Roto Pack Pvt Ltd already supplies identical laminates at ₹290.00/KG — a 1.7% gap we're paying above our own benchmark; the BOPET import line sits at 171.60 ₹/kg, well below our ₹295.00/KG landed cost

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (half our current 30-day cycle) in exchange for the ₹5/KG price reduction, framing it as a cash-flow benefit worth their 10.96% borrowing cost
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 15 days frees ₹9.49 L of our working capital; their borrowing cost is 10.96%, so early payment saves them roughly that rate on the accelerated cash

brief.financialLeverage: GLS Films is loss-making (net margin -3.4% vs peer median 2.5%) with a health score of D (21/100) and an Altman Z of 1.68 (grey zone). They carry debt at 2.15x equity and interest coverage of just 0.06x, flagged for EPF and GST delays and severe legal cases. Our ₹2.31 Cr spend is only 0.33% of their ₹691.05 Cr revenue, so we have no volume leverage. Push gently: frame the ask around faster payment (worth 10.96% to them) and committed volume in exchange for matching our best price, and quietly qualify Huhtamaki or UFLEX as a second source — a hard price cut alone could destabilise supply.

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets with ₹2611.64 Cr revenue

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant (₹16492.00 Cr revenue) covering both film substrate and conversion — can second-source laminates at scale

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Global Constantia group's India converter focused on pharma blister and sachet laminates — strong fit for GEEP sachets

risks: Loss-making (net margin -3.4%, PAT ₹-23.68 Cr) and grey-zone Altman Z (1.68) — pushing too hard on price alone could tip supply continuity
Multiple red flags: severe legal cases, GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, high leverage (2.15x), and a Probe42 score of 2/10 — qualify a second source before concentrating more volume here
We represent only 0.33% of their revenue, so we have no volume muscle; the ask must rest on fairness (matching our best price) and the cash value of faster payment
Their margin is already 5.9 percentage points below peers (-3.4% vs 2.5%), so a price cut bites harder here than at a healthy supplier — sweeten with volume commitment or faster cash
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in a multi-year volume commitment with you, but we need to close the gap to the ₹290.00/KG we already pay Shrinath Roto — and we're happy to cut our payment cycle in half to help your cash flow in return.
